draw.hint: For books with no cover in any catalog. AI writes a prompt from the book, then draws the cover.

identify.title: Lookup
identify.hint: Cover, title, author, year and ISBN, from Open Library and Google Books.

identify.none: No results. Try the full title, or add the author’s name.
identify.unreachable: Couldn’t reach the catalogs just now. That is not the same as the book not being there — try again in a moment.
identify.refused: Didn’t answer this time ({{reason}}). That is not the same as not having the book.
identify.needsKey: Google’s older feed didn’t answer either. Its current API needs a key of your own — free, and it is the catalog with most of what was published this century.

identify.keyStays: Kept in this phone’s keychain. Never in a backup, and sent to nobody but Google.
identify.keyWhere: Get one: Google Cloud console → enable the Books API → Credentials → Create API key.
identify.chineseIsbn: This is a Chinese ISBN (978-7-…). Both catalogs were asked and neither holds this printing — Open Library has a fraction of what China publishes. The surest way is the title in Chinese.

shelf.title: Shelf
shelf.unreadable: The library couldn’t be opened. Nothing is lost — your books are still on this device.
shelf.emptyHint: Tap the bar at the bottom to add one: a file, a link, a catalog, or just a title you remember.
shelf.fromLinkHint: A Google Doc, or any direct file URL
shelf.linkSignIn: That link requires signing in. Share it with “Anyone with the link”, or download the file and import it.
shelf.kindTitle: What kind of book is this?

reviews.title: Reviews
reviews.none: Nothing written about a book yet. A review is written on the book’s own page, under the stars.

import.title: Import
import.noText: No text found in this file.
import.unsupported: {{ext}} files aren’t read on the phone. Convert it on a computer first — `make pdf FILE=…` turns one into an EPUB, figures and all.
import.previewEmpty: No readable text was found. Scanned pages are images and can’t be read.

book.deleteConfirm: Delete this book? Its notes and highlights go with it — kept in Recently deleted for 30 days, then gone.
book.title: Title
book.author: Author
book.summaryPlaceholder: What is this book about? A few sentences.
book.aiSummarizeWhat: Writes a few sentences from the chapter briefs where they exist, and from the opening where they don’t. Yours is replaced, so copy it first if you want to keep it.
book.esvKeyHint: What the chapters are fetched with. Kept in the keychain on this device.
book.analyzeAllHint: People, places, scenes and continuity, chapter by chapter — one queued task each. Stop it part way and what finished is kept.
book.translateAllHint: Queues every chapter that still needs it. A sentence you correct afterwards teaches the ones after it.
book.translateAllDone: Every sentence is already translated into this language.
book.queueAllCost_one: {{count}} chapter, about {{cost}} in all — billed to your own key on {{vendor}}. An estimate, not a charge.
book.queueAllCost_other: {{count}} chapters, about {{cost}} in all — billed to your own key on {{vendor}}. An estimate, not a charge.
book.queueAllUnpriced_one: {{count}} chapter. Add an AI key to see what it would cost.
book.queueAllUnpriced_other: {{count}} chapters. Add an AI key to see what it would cost.
book.correctHint: Title, author, year and edition, as they should read.
book.correctWhat: Checks the title, author, year and edition against what’s known about this work and fixes any mistakes — a misremembered title, an author reduced to initials, a missing subtitle, a year off by one. It won’t translate the title or replace the book with a different one. If the work can’t be identified, it says so. One small request.
book.correctQueued: Queued. You can follow it in the queue.
book.summarizeWhat: Writes a summary of the book from the briefs its chapters already have. No text is sent and nothing is re-read, so it costs one small request no matter how long the book is.
book.summarizeQueued: Queued. You can follow it in the queue.
book.partsHint: Each part has its own page with its description, its chapters, and every note you made in it.
book.reviewPlaceholder: What did you make of it? A line or an essay — it saves itself.
book.lookUpWhat: Asks the model what it knows about this book — the author, the year and a few sentences on what it’s about. Only missing details are filled in. If the model doesn’t know the book, it says so instead of making things up.
book.outlineHint: A chapter list for a book that has no text here.
book.outlineWhat: Asks the model for this book’s table of contents — every chapter in order, each with a line on what it covers. Each chapter then gets its own page for notes. If the model doesn’t know the book, it says so.
book.outlineQueued: Queued. You can follow it in the queue.
book.outlineReplace: This replaces the {{count}} existing chapters, including any edits you made to them.
book.languageHint: What the book is written in. Every AI pass answers in it.
book.addTextFile: Add the text from a file
book.addTextWhat: The book goes on reading once its words are here. Nothing else about this record changes.
book.addTextLink: Add the text from a link
book.textSourceWhy: This book is a record so far. Give it a manuscript and it opens for reading.
book.textNoneFound: No kept list has this one. Fetch a list from the search page, or bring the file yourself.
book.wordsEmpty: Words and phrases you keep while reading show up here.

reader.hint: Tap any sentence to highlight, note or share it.
reader.notePlaceholder: What do you want to remember about this?
reader.shareCardHint: An image card in your reading theme.
reader.selectHint: Tap another sentence to extend the selection
reader.newCard: ＋ A new flash card from this
reader.newTerm: ＋ A new concept or term from this

settings.aiHint: Used for chapter detection and analysis. Keys stay on this device and are never included in backups.
settings.cloudHint: Storage you own. Off by default.
settings.backupHint: Survives a bad import or a corrupt database — not a lost phone. Copy the file off to keep it safe.
settings.aiGetOne: Don’t have a {{vendor}} key? Get one →
settings.aiBilling: Requests are billed to your own {{vendor}} account.
settings.aiStrategyHint: Keys are tried in the order listed. Sequential uses the first key until it fails; round robin rotates through all keys.
settings.privateCloudHint: Storage you own. Off by default.
settings.gradeHint_fast: 512 px on the older model. Fast and cheap, but follows the prompt loosely.
settings.gradeHint_normal: 1024 px on the current model, cheapest setting. Follows the prompt closely.
settings.gradeHint_best: 1024 px on the current model, slowest setting. Follows the prompt just as closely, with more detail.
settings.removeAllWarning: A full backup is saved on this device first — and to iCloud and any connected buckets, if set up. It holds everything but your keys: books, notes, translations, settings, even the files they were imported from. Deletion starts only after the backups finish; if a cloud backup fails, nothing is deleted.
settings.removeAllKeeps: The copy taken first stays in Files → Novel Man → Backups, and is not deleted with the rest.
settings.aiTimeout: {{vendor}} didn’t answer within 10 seconds. The key may be fine — a model this vendor has retired can hang instead of failing. Try another model.

flags.title: Flagged works
flags.rowWhy: Books missing a cover, an author, a year or their chapters
flags.allWell: Every book on your shelf has a cover, an author, a year and its chapters. Nothing to fix here.
flags.tocWhy: Nothing to turn: the import never found a table of contents. Detect them on the book’s structure page.
flags.oneChapterWhy: A book this long found as a single chapter almost always means none were found at all. Split it on the structure page.
flags.detailsWhy: No author, or no year. One lookup fills both — and no catalog can be asked about a book with no author.
flags.coverWhy: Nothing to recognise it by on the shelf. Look it up for a catalog cover, or have one drawn.

job.title: Downloading
job.working: This page stays open while the book downloads, and opens the book when it’s ready.
job.hint: You can leave this page. The download continues, and the shelf shows its progress.
job.failedHint: Nothing was added. Retry to send the same request again.

lookup.keyStaysHere: The key stays on this device. It’s never synced or backed up.
lookup.savedHint: Only passages you looked up, stored on this device only.
lookup.busy: Too many requests. Try again in a moment.
lookup.rejected: That key was rejected. Check it at api.esv.org.
lookup.offline: Couldn’t reach api.esv.org. Check your connection.

entity.noRenderings: No names in other languages yet.
entity.name: Name
entity.summaryPlaceholder: Who is this person, in a line or two?
entity.timelineFetched: Counted from the text stored on this device. This edition is fetched a chapter at a time, so the graph shows where you’ve read rather than everywhere they appear.
entity.polishWhat: Combines {{count}} chapter notes about this person into a profile: summary, role, appearance, voice and arc. The chapter notes stay as they are, so you can run it again or check what it was based on.
entity.tapToRead: Tap a line to read that passage in the book.
entity.relationSearch: Search people, or type a new name
entity.relationEmpty: No other people in this book yet.

notes.empty: Highlights and notes you make while reading show up here.
notes.selectHint: Tap the ones you want to delete.
notes.deleteSelectedConfirm: Delete {{count}} items? The text in the book isn’t affected.
notes.emptyRecord: No notes yet. Tap ＋ to write one about this book.

structure.deleteWhere: Its text will be merged into a neighboring chapter. Which one?
structure.title: Structure
structure.unsureCount: {{count}} chapters were detected with low confidence.
structure.redetectConfirm: Detect chapters again? Chapters you renamed keep their names.
structure.redetectHint: Your renames and splits are kept; everything else is recalculated.
structure.splitHint: The sentence you pick becomes the start of the new chapter. ¶ marks the start of a paragraph.
structure.noSplitPoints: This chapter is a single paragraph — there’s nowhere to split it.
structure.aiDetectWhat: Sends only the short lines that might be headings — never the full text — and asks which ones are chapters. Your renames are kept.
structure.aiFoundNothing: No chapters found. Nothing was changed.
structure.deleteConfirm: Its text is merged into the neighboring chapter. Nothing is removed from the book.
structure.aiScenes: Suggest scene breaks in every chapter
structure.aiScenesWhat: Sends the first line of each paragraph — never the full text — and asks where the time, place or point of view changes. Scene breaks you already marked are overwritten.
structure.aiChapterBrief: Write this chapter’s brief with AI
structure.aiOneWhat: Reads this one chapter with the book’s summary, the chapters just before it, and everyone already known as context. Writes its brief, its people, its places and the ties between them.
structure.aiOneBriefWhat: One or two sentences on what happens, written with the chapters just before it as context.
structure.addChapterHint: Added at the end without a title. Open it to name it and add notes.
structure.recordHint: There’s no text to split here, so chapters are either typed by you or supplied by the model. Briefs come from what the model knows of the book, and it says so when it doesn’t know it.

backup.title: Backup
backup.icloudOff: iCloud Drive is off on this device
backup.icloudDirections: Settings → your name → iCloud → iCloud Drive → turn on
backup.icloudUnsigned: This build of the app isn’t signed for iCloud.
backup.icloudNotReady: iCloud is still setting up. Try again in a moment.
backup.icloudBrowseHint: The ten most recent backups are kept. Restoring adds books alongside the ones you have; nothing is overwritten.
backup.nowUnchanged: Nothing has changed since the last backup.
backup.restoredWaiting: {{count}} books came back as skeletons — everything but the text.
backup.restoreConfirm: Restoring adds books. Nothing already here is overwritten.
backup.duplicates: Already on your shelf, so restored as copies: {{list}}
backup.notABundle: That isn’t a Novel Man backup.
backup.tooNew: This backup was made by a newer version (v{{version}}). Update the app first.
backup.aboutUnknown: Written by an older version, which didn’t record what was in it. Restoring still works.
backup.repaired: Put {{count}} missing covers back on books already on your shelf.

copies.title: Your copies
copies.promise: Your library is a database and a folder of files inside this app, and every copy of it is a .zip anyone can open: library.csv for the shelf, a notes file per book you annotated, and the books themselves. Nothing in a copy needs this app to be read, and none of it needs an account. Never in a copy: your AI keys and bucket secrets, which stay in this phone’s keychain.
copies.promiseShort: Every copy is a .zip you can open anywhere, holding a plain library.csv beside the rest. Keys never travel.
copies.icloudFailed: The last copy to iCloud didn’t go up
copies.nothingLeaves: Nothing is being copied off this phone. The copies below are instant and offline, and they are deleted with the app.
copies.onPhoneHint: Files → On My iPhone → Novel Man → Backups. Tap one to send it somewhere else. These survive a mistake, not a lost or wiped phone.
copies.kind_daily: The whole library, once a day
copies.kind_guard: Taken before something rewrote a lot at once
copies.icloudCount: {{count}} copies kept in your iCloud Drive
copies.icloudOff: Off — no copy leaves this phone
copies.bucketHint: Your own bucket, where every copy is kept
copies.bundleHint: One .zip that can restore all of it, down to the files your books came from
copies.exportPlainHint: library.csv and a notes file per book. Readable in anything, no restore needed.
copies.restoreHint: Any copy above, or any .zip you kept. One book out of it, or all of them.
copies.keptHint: Still here, in Files → Novel Man → exports.
copies.stateEmpty: Nothing on the shelf to copy yet
copies.stateHereOnly: {{count}} copies, all of them on this phone
copies.stateBehind: Changes that have not left this phone yet
copies.logHint: Every copy taken, and what was in it

covers.sweptWhat:
These were wearing Google’s “image not available” picture, which an older lookup kept by mistake. They are back to their own tiles — look one up again for a real cover.

covers.lostWhat:

trash.title: Recently deleted
trash.why: A deleted book waits here for {{days}} days with its notes, highlights, people and reading dates — as a file in Files → Novel Man → Trash. Putting one back restores all of it.
trash.what: Put this book back on the shelf, or delete it for good?
trash.fileGone: The file for this book isn’t there any more.
trash.empty: Delete all of these for good
trash.emptyWarning: These books and their notes go for good. A backup taken before they were deleted still holds them.

safe.offerTitle: Keep a copy off this phone?
safe.offerWhat: Your books, notes and progress go to your own iCloud Drive whenever they change — so deleting the app, or losing the phone, doesn’t take them with it. Nothing goes anywhere else, and your keys never leave this device.
safe.foundWhat: A backup from {{when}} is in your iCloud Drive.
safe.cameBack: {{chapters}} chapters and {{notes}} notes came back with them.

ai.noKey: No AI key configured. Add one in Settings first.
ai.noEstimate: Add a key to see the estimated cost.
ai.estimateHint: An estimate, not an exact price. Billed to your own account. Results are cached, so running it again is free.
ai.estimateNoKey: add an AI key to see the cost
ai.estimateForCited: {{action}} · est. {{tokens}} tokens · {{cost}} — sends the title, where this chapter sits in the book, and what the shelf already knows. There’s no text here to send.

cast.hint: Each pass reads the book once and caches the result, so running it again only costs for the parts that changed.
cast.what_relations: Asks how people who appear in the same chapters are connected. Sends profiles, not the book text.
cast.what_continuity: Compares what different chapters say about the same person and flags contradictions. Flags are suggestions to review; nothing is edited.
cast.extracted: {{characters}} people across the book. {{failed}} chapters failed.
cast.graphHint: Tap a person to show only their relationships. Hold to open their profile. Drag to move the graph.
cast.clearConfirm: Removes AI-generated profiles, appearances, relationships and flags. Profiles you wrote yourself are kept.

translate.empty: Add a language to translate this book into. Nothing is sent until you run the translation.
translate.mappingShort: Names and terms the translation must use.
translate.fromChapter: Translated a chapter at a time, from the chapter you are reading.
translate.nothingYet: Nothing translated in this chapter yet.
translate.editHint: Tap a sentence to correct it. Corrections are used as examples for the sentences that follow, and can be turned into terms.
translate.converted: Converted {{count}} sentences on this phone — 简体 and 繁體 are the same words in another script, so no model was asked and nothing was sent.
translate.readInReader: Read it in the reader. Choose the language from the Aa menu.
translate.promoteHint: Terms apply in every chapter. Sentences already translated with this word are marked for re-translation.
translate.termAffects: {{count}} translated sentences use it and are marked for re-translation.
translate.termsHint: Every term here is used exactly as written, throughout the translation. ✨ suggests a translation for each name that has none — review and correct the drafts before saving.
translate.someFailed: Kept the {{count}} that succeeded. The rest failed with: {{error}}
translate.proposedHint: Nothing is saved yet. Fix any mistakes, remove what you don’t want, then keep or reject them all.
translate.nothingToFill: Every term here already has a translation.
translate.candidates: Found in the text, not yet added
translate.candidatesHint: Names and recurring proper nouns found in the book. Tap one to add it above and give it a translation.
translate.removeConfirm: Delete the {{language}} translation, including your edits?

cloud.title: Where copies go
cloud.hint: Every backup holds everything but your keys — books, notes, translations, people, progress, settings and the files you imported. iCloud keeps the last ten copies; your own bucket keeps every one, and nothing is uploaded there until you ask.
cloud.addConnectionHint: Your own S3-compatible bucket, for full backups with history.
cloud.name: Name
cloud.pasteHint: Paste credentials from a console page, an .env file or a CSV row, and the fields fill in automatically.
cloud.saveHint: Saving sends a test request. If the bucket can’t be listed, the connection isn’t saved.
cloud.frequencyHint: Manual by default. Automatic sync runs when you open the app, never in the background.
cloud.getHint: Downloading a backup restores it the same way a file does: books are added, nothing is overwritten.
cloud.removeConfirm: Removes the connection and its key from this device. The bucket’s contents are not affected.
cloud.unreachable: Couldn’t reach {{host}}. Nothing was wrong with your keys — no server answered. Check the endpoint and the region, and that the phone is online.
cloud.endpoint_empty: This provider needs an endpoint address.
cloud.endpoint_gap: That works out to {{endpoint}}, which is not a real address — a region or account is missing above.
cloud.endpoint_insecure: iOS refuses plain http addresses. Use https, or an address with a certificate.

script.hint: Converted one scene at a time, so the scene breaks from the structure editor become the screenplay’s scenes.
script.what: Turns each scene into slug lines, action and dialogue. Inner thoughts are rewritten as what a camera could see — that’s a real rewrite, so read it before using it.
script.clearConfirm: Deletes the screenplay. The novel isn’t affected.

work.title: Analysis queue
work.hint: Tasks keep running while you read, and resume where they left off if you close the app. Finished chapters are kept even if you stop a run.
work.queued: Queued {{count}} chapters. Progress shows on the shelf.
work.task_book-outline: Get the table of contents for {{what}}

chapter.scriptHint: This book’s scenes as a screenplay.

chapter.noTerms: No terms recognized in this chapter.

scenes.title: Scenes
scenes.emptyHint: Scenes come from analyzing a chapter, or from marking scene breaks yourself in the chapter list. None are guessed at import.

card.frontPlaceholder: The front — what you want to be asked
card.backPlaceholder: The description — what you want to recall, in your own words.
card.excerptHint: Tap a passage to read it where it was written. Press and hold to take it off this card.
card.addHint: While reading, select a sentence and choose “File this…” to put it on this card.
card.hint: A card is yours: nothing here is written or rewritten by a pass over the book.
card.deleteConfirm: Delete this card? The passages on it go too; the book and your highlights are untouched.

study.title: Flash cards
study.nothingKept: Nothing kept from this book yet. Cards, terms and words you keep all end up here.
study.nothingDue: Nothing due. Come back when the schedule says so — studying early is how spacing stops working.
study.noBacks: Nothing here has a meaning written on it yet, so there is nothing to check a recall against.

ol.searchLive: A title or author, then press return
ol.hintKept: Everything in your saved categories. Type to filter.
ol.hintLive: Searches openlibrary.org live. Requires a connection.
ol.categoriesHint: A category is downloaded once and searched on this device after that — no connection needed.
ol.getFailed: Couldn’t reach openlibrary.org. Your saved categories still work.
ol.noLists: No categories saved yet. Download one below, or search all of Open Library.
ol.whatYouGet: Adding a book gives you its record — title, author, year and cover — not the text.

gr.noApi: Goodreads shut down its API in 2020, so no app can sign in on your behalf. What is still public is your profile’s feed and the library export — both carry your ratings, reviews, shelves and dates read.
gr.how1: goodreads.com › My Books › Import and export › Export Library, then choose the CSV here.
gr.how1Detail: Goodreads emails you a CSV, or shows a download link on that page. Save it to Files, then choose it here.
gr.notAnExport: No books found in that file. Make sure it’s the library export, not the reviews export.
gr.feedWhy: Unlike an export file, this can be read again whenever your shelves change.
gr.feedHint: Open your profile in a browser and copy the address — that is all this needs. A shelf link works too, and so does an RSS address if you have one. Nothing is signed in to; a public profile’s feed is public.
gr.notAFeed: That is not a Goodreads profile or shelf address.
gr.emptyFeed: That profile listed no books. If it is set to private, paste the RSS address instead — it carries a key.
gr.feedFailed: Couldn’t read that profile. Check the address, or use the export file.
gr.whatHappens: Each book becomes a shelf entry without text, with its rating, review, shelf and private notes. Books already on your shelf have missing details filled in rather than being added twice, and nothing you wrote is overwritten.
gr.filledHint: Already on the shelf; missing details were filled in from the export.
gr.savedForget: Stop offering this shelf here? Nothing already imported is touched.

csv.why: A library from anywhere, as a CSV. Goodreads’ own export is read as it stands; any other file works too, as long as its header row carries the columns below.
csv.how: Goodreads writes one from Settings › Import and export. Douban publishes no export, so tools/douban-shelf.py in this repo makes one from your shelf pages: python3 tools/douban-shelf.py <your Douban id>. Anything else — another app, a spreadsheet of your own — needs only these column names. Save the file to Files, then choose it here.
csv.notACsv: No books found in that file. Check its header row against the columns below.

col.title: The title, as the shelf shows it
col.id: The id the platform knows the book by, so importing twice updates rather than duplicates
col.author: The author, or the first name on the publisher line
col.shelf: read, currently-reading or to-read — 读过, 在读 and 想读 also work
col.rating: 1 to 5, or 0 where you never rated it
col.review: What you wrote about it, kept as the review
col.isbn: What finds a cover and the right edition later

gallery.title: Gallery
gallery.queued: Added to the queue. You can leave this page; it keeps going.

timeline.title: Reading timeline
timeline.empty: Nothing yet. Setting a status, finishing a chapter or importing from Goodreads writes here — or add a moment yourself.
timeline.notePlaceholder: What happened — bought it, lent it out, gave up on page 40…
timeline.badDayHint: Write it as 2026-09-25 — year, month, day.
timeline.removeWhat: Remove this from the timeline? The book itself is untouched.

log.title: Backup history
log.hint: Every copy this app has taken, newest first. The bundles themselves are named for a day, rewritten all day, and only the last ten are kept — so this is the part that remembers the rest. The most recent 1,000 entries stay here.
log.empty: No copy has been taken yet.

language.fixedWhat:
A catalog answered these in romanised Latin, so they were filed as English — and English is what every AI pass was told to answer in. They now say what they are written in.
